newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures rise on pre-holiday covering.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures rise on pre-holiday covering.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended higher on Friday as players covered their positions ahead of a long weekend in Japan and the release of the U.S. non-farm payrolls report at 1230 GMT.
The lead Nikkei 225 June contract ended 210 points higher at 19,570 on light volume of 12,080 lots.
Dealers said trading was thin and technically driven, with Nikkei futures gaining on the back of weakness in Japanese government bond and Euroyen futures.
"It was just short-covering ahead of the weekend. People are very cautious ahead of the payrolls number," a senior trader with an Asian institution said.
"The undertone is moving in line with the New York stock market," he said, adding that the June Nikkei looked well supported around 19,200-19,250.
He said the market was likely to face resistance initially at 19,700.
Taiwan stock index futures ended sharply lower in line with a steep drop in Taipei stocks as concern about the earnings outlook of leading blue chip counters depressed sentiment.
The May MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 337.7 against its opening 350.0 on volume of 1,505 lots.
